conventions.convention: The fixed-design noise proxy bounds every directional MGF by exp(σ²λ²‖u‖₂²/2); coordinate independence is not assumed.
The Lasso objective is ‖y−Xθ‖₂²/n + 2τ‖θ‖₁, with τ strictly positive. The definition specifies the entire minimizer set and selects no measurable minimizer.
Incoherence means max-entry deviation of XᵀX/n from I at most 1/(14s), including diagonal deviations.
The cone is ‖v outside S‖₁ ≤ 3‖v on S‖₁; the restricted eigenvalue lower bound uses ‖v on S‖₂², for every support of size at most s.
Both covariance estimators use divisor n. Oracle centering uses the population mean; sample centering uses the empirical mean. Loss is squared operator norm.

Weak-lq sparsity concerns off-diagonal columns only. For 0<q<1, k times the qth power of the kth ordered magnitude is at most c; q=0 instead counts nonzero off-diagonal entries. The directional tail has prefactor 1: P(|vᵀ(X−EX)|>t) ≤ exp(−t²/(2τ)).
Thresholding preserves every diagonal entry and retains an off-diagonal entry at threshold equality. Its output is symmetric but need not be positive semidefinite.

Minimax risk ranges over measurable maps into the full Euclidean Borel matrix space, including nonsymmetric outputs, under the n-fold product sample law. Infinite risk is permitted; the supremum over an empty law class is zero.
Gaussian covariance KL is directional, with Σ₁ inverse multiplying Σ₀ and log(det Σ₁/det Σ₀); both matrices must be positive definite. AC is inherited through the Gaussian and KL conventions.

The minimax equivalence is capped at min{1,c²(log p/n)^(1−q)+log p/n}. Raw thresholding has its stated expected-risk guarantee when log p/n≤1; the globally capped upper bound uses a threshold-or-zero switch.

load_bearing.statement: For p≥2, 0≤q<1, c≥0 and τ>0, the law class consists of laws with the stated off-diagonal weak-lq covariance constraint and P(|vᵀ(X−EX)|>t)≤exp(−t²/(2τ)) for every unit v and t>0; q=0 counts nonzero off-diagonal entries.
For a symmetric real p×p matrix with p≥1, its operator norm equals the maximum absolute unit-vector Rayleigh quotient and the largest absolute eigenvalue.
For iid observations from the specified class, n≥1, p≥2 and u>0, sample-centered covariance has maximum entrywise error at most 192τ(√(u/n)+u/n) with probability at least 1−2p exp(−u)−2p² exp(−2u).
If Σ belongs to Gq(c), threshold λ>0 is used, and every sample-centered covariance entry has error at most λ/2, then operator error is at most Cq(cλ^(1−q)+λ); C0=2 is admissible.

Assume AC and fix τ,M>0, β>1 and 0≤q<1. There exist v,b>0 and finite P0 depending only on these parameters such that, for p≥P0, n≥1, p≥n^β and 0≤c≤M n^((1−q)/2)(log p)^(-(3−q)/2), setting a=log p/n, s=τ/4 and ε=v√a, the condition c/[2(sε)^q]≥2 implies minimax risk at least b c²a^(1−q). For q=0, (sε)^q=1.

Fix τ>0, 0≤q<1 and β>1. For n≥1, p≥2, p≥n^β and a=log p/n≤1, the unmodified sample-centered threshold estimator with λ=8192τ√a has supremum expected squared operator error at most C(q,τ)(c²a^(1−q)+a).
Assume AC. For every n≥1, p≥2, τ>0, 0≤q<1 and c≥0, minimax squared operator risk over the specified law class is at least bτ² min{1,log p/n}, for an absolute b>0.
For positive-definite real symmetric p×p matrices, p≥1, under the Gaussian and directional KL conventions, D(Np(0,Σ₀)‖Np(0,Σ₁)) = [tr(Σ₁⁻¹Σ₀)−p+log(det Σ₁/det Σ₀)]/2.
For any Lasso minimizer with τ>0, support S of θ*, and Δ=θ̂−θ*, the score condition ‖Xᵀε/n‖∞≤τ/2 implies ‖XΔ‖₂²/n+τ‖Δ outside S‖₁≤3τ‖Δ on S‖₁, hence the cone constraint.
For n≥1 and 1≤s≤d, the stated incoherence condition implies ‖Xv‖₂²/n≥‖v on S‖₂²/2 for every support of size at most s and every v in its Lasso cone.

concerns.concern: The final Remark says, “The current planned theorem uses only the lower dimension condition” and says a cap “is needed before a minimax equivalence of this form can hold.” The current thm-thresholded-sparse-covariance-minimax-rate already states and proves the capped equivalence. Update this historical wording to identify the uncapped claim being refuted; the counterexample itself remains valid.

alerts.finding: The Statement begins “Let f and (f_n) be measurable complex-valued functions” and subsequently uses integrals against μ, but neither Statement nor Given binds a domain, sigma-algebra, or measure μ. Proof 1.1 also uses X without introducing it. Bind an arbitrary measure space (X,A,μ). The batch-19 applications supply their probability space and prove an integrable majorant before applying the result, so this declaration omission does not invalidate those uses.

seams_checked.note: The all-directions MGF proxy, finite-maximum tail without coordinate independence, zero-proxy clause, restricted-range sub-exponential sum bound, and sphere-net cardinality match the actual local uses. Independence is imposed across observations where sum concentration requires it.
This is contextual page preparation. No assigned item imports a symmetrization, contraction, or entropy result from that page, and no stronger proposition is attributed to it.

The Gaussian KL derivation preserves the directional density-ratio convention. The diagonal lower bound supplies measurable full-matrix actions, p+1 separated Gaussian targets, finite-product KL, and the reference-law average KL required by Fano. The sparse-mixture lemma proves its affinity and bit-testing argument locally rather than attributing them to generic Fano or Assouad.

The clean dense, clean single-block sparse, and contamination-modulus lower-bound consumers quote the positive-definite Gaussian trace-determinant KL formula with the correct direction. Their actual KL calculations use positive-definite covariance pairs; they do not extend that formula to singular pairs or identify the single-block class with weak row sparsity.
